s0001: Use a food chain diagram to correctly identify which animal is the predator and which is its prey
s0002: An arrow shows where the food goes: the living thing at the start of the arrow is the prey, and the animal the arrow points to is the predator that eats it. A predator and its prey are next to each other in the chain.

Which pair correctly shows a predator and its prey?

s0016: The animal the arrow points to is the one that eats. So it is the predator.
s0017: lizard → snake: the snake's prey is the lizard
s0018: There is an arrow from the lizard to the snake. So the snake hunts the lizard.

s0024: A student who chose B thought a plant can also be a predator; grass does not eat animals, it is only food.
s0025: A student who chose C found the right pair but swapped their roles: the eagle eats the snake.
s0026: Notice which animal the arrow points to — that animal is the one eating.

s0051: Know that condensation is the change of a substance from a gas (water vapor) into a liquid

s0057: a solid changing into a liquid

s0219: Understand that an object's weight depends not only on its size but also on the material it is made of, and give a reasoned argument against a wrong idea
s0220: If you can find an example of an object that is large but light (or small but heavy), you can see that the idea “a bigger object is always heavier” is wrong.

The teacher placed three objects on the table in order of size, from largest to smallest: a large pillow stuffed with cotton, a brick, and an apple.
Sardor said, “A bigger object is always heavier.”
Which statement is correct?
s0222: Sardor is right: the pillow is the biggest, so it is the heaviest.
s0223: Sardor is not right: the smallest object is always the heaviest.
s0224: Sardor is right: the apple is the smallest, so it is the lightest, and this proves his idea.
s0225: Sardor is not right: the pillow is lighter than the brick even though it is bigger, because weight also depends on the material an object is made of.
s0227: The objects are arranged in this order by size.
s0228: Inside the pillow — cotton and a lot of air
s0229: The pillow is big, but it is filled with light cotton and air.
s0231: The brick is smaller than the pillow, but if we pick it up, it is much heavier.
s0232: Weight also depends on the material
s0233: So a big object is not always heavy — Sardor's idea is wrong.
s0235: The correct explanation is option D.
s0236: A student who chose A thought size and weight are the same thing and did not consider what the pillow is made of.
